tips.text: Hard work is important, but preparing smart for an interview is also really important, reading through interview experiences and prepping accordingly is important.
There is a high possibility that even though you are the smartest, you might not end up with a good offer, and that's alright because placement has a huge chunk of luck on your side.
Be true to yourself; copying projects or lying won't land you anywhere. Consistent knowledge building over time is essential.
Keep your mind open during interviews so you can think of new examples and answers; when the interviewer reaches your strongest point, dive deep into it.
Consistently do DSA; in the last 1‑2 months you can prepare for other stuff.
Make your projects with a purpose, and if not, keep an answer ready that ties the project to a real‑world scenario.
Losing hope and feeling demotivated is normal; believe in yourself, stay fit, eat well and sleep well during the preparation period.

tips.text: Time management is very important in the first 2 sections. Questions are doable but the decision to attempt or skip a particular question based upon time is more important.
Many python users faced issues in this round and this was seen in PhonePe as well, so if you’ve enough time consider shifting to cpp/java.
Make sure you are clear with the basics of your first language and have some idea of OOP in Java too if java isn’t your first language. Also never ignore OOP in your first language.
Candidates whose first language is Java were also asked about development in Java (Springboot related) so be prepared.
Design problems are to check how you approach a problem so take your time and think in 360 degree, ask genuine questions related to company tech at the end.
Yes surprisingly most of us were never asked about DSA problems.
For all your projects make a google doc with all the important points/features, their implementation and tech stack as it becomes really easy to revise.
Add to it what problems did you face and how did you resolve them as it is a check question if you’ve done the project yourself.
Whenever you feel confused, communicate with the interviewer, they’ll surely help you out.
Try to connect answers with company values. Read about their vision/mission, tagline, history.
There might be some trick questions which play on our psychology so it is always safer to answer honestly.
Be friendly with the interviewer and reflect your true personality.
Prepare basics really well, not being able to answer them gives a bad impression.
Don’t consider DSA as the only way to conquer placements. Balance dev/DSA and start revising core subjects early.
Basic web dev projects won’t be enough; explore basics of devops or app dev.
Many companies were asking LLD/system design, so allocate time to these topics.
Give mock interviews with friends or seniors to build confidence and identify weak sections.
Never let rejections bring you down; focus on what you can control.
Get an internship even if it's unpaid!!!
Consider learning LLD/system design early on.

tips.text: Time management is the most important aspect of an OA. You must attempt easy and especially short questions first and then go to longer ones. Understand what the question is asking before jumping to the answer and sometimes just try option elimination if nothing works.

Keep 30-45 seconds at the end reserved for unattempted questions. This time is basically for those questions that you have absolutely no idea how to answer. You quickly select random options for these and since there are no -ve marks make sure to attempt each question.
For aptitude questions refer to IndiaBix and make sure to study up on statistics formulas as they are usually asked in IDFC OAs.

For the coding section, the questions for any company are never straightforward; they will give some kind of a pointless story which will take you a minute or two to read and some more minutes to comprehend. These won’t be your typical LeetCode questions. I would suggest that toward the end of your preparation phase practice a few of these questions by asking ChatGPT to generate such lengthy story based company OA style questions.
Make ChatGPT your friend as there is no better tool for interview preparations.

Know your resume forwards and backwards without missing a single piece of information. Also prepare for in-depth questions for each part of the resume. Sometimes an interview might take a point in your resume and ask very in-depth questions to test your understanding. Use ChatGPT for this and ask it to give curveball questions too.

Make sure to keep the points in your resume as honest as possible and don’t mention something you lack understanding in. If extremely necessary to include a part you might not know about, make sure to understand it in-depth one day before the interview. Keep in mind that the interviewer is sitting with a laptop and you’re not.

I would advise that you learn OOPs concepts in Java as a lot of companies have Java as a requirement or at least have some projects of Java in their systems. Then learn those same concepts in your preferred language.
For each language you mention in your resume, go through its interview questions from GFG because a lot of times they cover almost everything about the language.

Technical Interviews are as much a psychological game as they are about your technical skills. The interviewers will ask you questions on what you have mentioned in your resume and based on what you answer. Make sure to drop hints of where you want to lead them. A lot of the time they might end up asking exactly that.

Be confident and honest in your answers and if you are asked something you don’t know or to write a code whose syntax you do not recall, try explaining the concept and approach and related concepts you know. Most of the time that is what interviewers are looking for. If there comes a point where you have absolutely no clue of what you are asked, just be straight with them and say that you haven’t learnt or worked with this particular concept instead of making up a useless explanation.

This is to be followed for all interviews and this is one of the most important aspects of an interview, keep a good eye contact with the interviewer. This might not seem like anything but it conveys that you are confident in your abilities and your answers, otherwise you come across as underconfident especially during HR interviews.

Prepare a clear introduction of yourself well before the interviews. Don't ever think that you can wing it, but at the same time do not rote the intro, prepare points that you want to convey and define a clear flow.

Keep your introduction short but make it a story where each point connects to the next and relate it to the role. Also set clear boundaries about what you do and don’t know in the intro itself. For example I had used Python for ML and data projects, C++ for DSA and recently learnt Java only for OOPs so I made this very clear in the introduction. This ensures that the interviewer doesn’t ask you anything out of scope. The more generalized your introduction is, the more curveballs you could potentially face.

Think of HR round as a chess match where you have to constantly think, react and plan ahead for every move you make, with the addition that your moves are being constantly judged. My interviewer was someone who was in the HR industry for 15 years and yours would also probably be someone with the same experience so they know people very well, so always be on your guard and say things that actually do align with what you believe in.

Be honest but not too honest. This might seem confusing but HR representatives can usually identify when you’re lying very easily. Now for the not too honest part, whatever you answer though the actual reason might be something else, mention that, but additionally connect it to the company’s values and requirements. For example, for the work from home question some of you might prefer that but the company has work from office policy so align your answer such that you believe in work from home but are open to work from office.

Align your answers with the company values and your own experiences. Why this is important is because when you just state facts as an answer but you connect it with an actual experience, it becomes a story which always has great value in interviews not just HR but technical ones too.

Another important tip which will help you navigate HR easily is not to keep it one way where they ask and you answer. Try keeping it two-way where you ask them questions based on their questions and your answers and if you are confident enough try adding in a funny remark or two to make the atmosphere less tense.

Remember the names of your previous interviewers as it might be asked during HR and it is also a good practice to know it if you do get selected. Usually each interviewer introduces themselves at the start itself but in case someone does not, make it a practice to ask their names at the end of the interview.

Let's start with the preparation phase before the placement season. The most important part is DSA this will help you clear a lot of Online Assessments for all the major companies. Start as early as possible, the earlier the better. Also what is more important than starting early is maintaining consistency. I was one of the first people to start DSA during the start of 3rd year but then left it midway for almost the entire Sem 5. Do not make this mistake, once you start make it a habit to do DSA everyday even if it is just one question.

You can follow a sheet like Striver’s A2Z Sheet or NeetCode or do a combination of both like I did. Start with Striver’s SDE Sheet or NeetCode 150 whichever you are comfortable with if you feel confident about Data Structures or go for A2Z Sheet or NeetCode 250 if your basics aren’t clear. For Recursion, DP and Graphs make sure to strictly follow Striver and his respective playlists on the topics as it is the best resource on the internet for these topics. The rest you can do from either.

Another aspect of DSA is explaining your approach. You may be amazing at DSA but if you cannot explain your approach none of it is any use. When practicing LeetCode, although this might take additional time, but try explaining your approach in your head while you are solving the question

Try to do LeetCode contests if you have the time or you complete DSA early enough to practice time management and make sure to practice company style story based questions for OA practice using ChatGPT. You can also experiment with CP if you enjoy doing LeetCode and DSA although I wouldn’t recommend it for those of y’all who are doing it for the sake of placements like I was.

Next comes SQL, this may seem like an easy topic but this is very crucial as it is asked in almost all interviews. Start with a basic crash course of SQL like Apna College or some other channel to learn basic topics like GROUP BY, ORDER BY, SELECT, JOINS and other basics. Once you have a basic understanding of these jump directly to SQL 50 from LeetCode as the more you practice the better you will be. For each question in SQL 50 if you don’t get the solution, go through the solutions of other people or the editorial by LeetCode if given. Do not directly move to ChatGPT that won’t help you understand and explore.

For OOPS follow Kunal Kuswaha’s playlist for OOPs that is the best there is. There is nothing additional required. If you are also working with some other language like C++ or Python refer to OOPs in those languages through ChatGPT and Google. Do preparation for OOPs toward the end of the preparation phase with 2-3 weeks left for the placement season so as to remember the concepts better. After all of this try doing some OS and CCN if time permits.

I would recommend doing an internship or two and if you have already done one, make sure to present it well in your resume as this carries a lot of weight. It basically shows the interviewer that other companies also decided to work with you and you have already worked in a professional environment. Even if you do not have an internship, add 3-4 good and diverse projects in your resume so that you can stand out from the crowd. Keep in mind that everyone is going to do normal web dev projects, so to stand you must do different projects that integrate multiple things and try to do a project that includes an AI workflow.

Make sure that you know each of your resume projects inside out and you can talk about them for hours with the interviewer. Try to only add projects that you have actually worked on and even if you do add a project right from the internet which I wouldn’t recommend but in extreme cases if you do make sure that you put it into ChatGPT or CoPilot and know every aspect of it.

Now for the interview part, once you clear the OA try to get a good night’s sleep before the interview day but in case it is your first interview and you have a habit and can manage with less sleep, I would recommend that you prepare well the night before if there is something you haven’t. Again I would only recommend this if you have done it a lot of times over the years during exams. I did this exact thing and I was a bit sleepy on the D-Day but it was worth it otherwise I wouldn’t have been well prepared, so manage your risk accordingly.

On the day of the interview, there can be a possibility that your interview might be scheduled later in the day so during this time keep talking to people around you or do some last minute revision but do not overthink and get tensed about your interview. Even if your friends aren’t with you, talk to other people so that you get engaged and it takes the edge off.

Lastly remember that no matter how much you prepare there will always be situations that work against you like curveball questions you hadn’t expected or a stubborn interviewer or any other situation that you did not expect so always be ready for such things. Also be mentally prepared to face ample rejections before you even get an interview or get placed. I got my first interview after facing more than 6-7 OAs and faced 3 interviews before I got placed and for each of these I managed to reach the final round and then got rejected. Keep in mind that this is a part of the placement proces and always be ready to get up and move on.

tips.text: I recommend practicing aptitude and do not skip it like I did because solving aptitude along with DSA will help you get an edge over others.

Do leetcode, codeforces, codechef or any other platform that you like, DO NOT skip over any advanced DSA topic however difficult it may seem (cost me my phonepe interview had I known lifting beforehand). Solving advanced DSA problems helps you build the instinct where you do not have to put efforts into coming up with a solution.

I would suggest when you are definitely clear with the answer, make some stories and tell, do not tell directly, this allows you to cover time and list down some extra points in front of the interviewer which many candidates would not have mentioned had they been in a hurry.
For the technical round, I would suggest having a strong knowledge of the CS fundamentals and programming languages on your finger tips.
Be calm in the interview and answer every question to the point, by making some stories to sugarcoat your answer.
If you absolutely know the answer to a question, cook the response as much as you can, do not give straightforward answers like some AI or a robot.
Keep your theory knowledge crisp with reasons for every fact, you need to know what is happening and why something is made in a certain way.
Be prepared to face tougher situations as the purpose of further rounds is to test how mentally strong you are.
DO NOT MELT IN FRONT OF THE INTERVIEWER HOWEVER RUDE OR UNINTERESTED THEY MAY SEEM.
If the interviewer interrupts you in between, take it as a positive point because you were already on the right track and they got it, that is why they change the questions.
Have confidence in yourself and do not underestimate yourself, if you are sure of something then do argue with the interviewer, sometimes they are also at fault.
Prepare for the HR round by chatGPT.
They ask pretty standard questions and you are expected to give their standard answers as well, like a viva.
Try to stay calm and smile in front of the HR
Be ready for surprises as this round was not initially planned.
Also do not assume that if you have come this far then it is absolutely guaranteed that you will get selected, as one candidate was not selected after these 4 rigorous interview rounds.
Start early with DSA and development. It gives you a very strong edge over others.
Do not be stuck in the “Dev or DSA” hell. YOU MUST HAVE BOTH OF THEM AT A PRETTY GOOD LEVEL.
Nowadays everybody knows the MERN stack and it has become the new normal, do not limit yourself to only one technology. Explore other technologies as well like Java Development, Spring boot, etc.
Make some projects which actually solve real world problems, not just a CRUD application with some eye-catching UI which is made by vercel v0 or claude.

Participate in hackathons and solve their problem statements, even if you cannot win the hackathon do not stop building the application for the problem. You will anyways have a solid project with you if you keep on working with the statement.

Do not ignore system design. It is now becoming common to ask system design to freshers and may happen that it will become a part of your process like DSA. At least know the basics of HLD, LLD and have a knowledge about the famous questions of system design.

Give leetcode/codeforces/codechef/atcoder contests, they help you keep your mind in the correct momentum which is needed during the placement season. You cannot stop your mind midway through the season.

Having internships with proper firms gives you an edge, because nowadays everybody has some kind of internship experience. If you do not have an internship, then you have to work a little more to compete with the ones having internships.
Do not get inferiority complex with the people who have summer internships or any other. Hard work and consistency makes a lot of difference.
DO NOT EXPECT THE PLACEMENT SEASON TO BE VERY SMOOTH. You have to be mentally strong for this and rejections are a part of it.
Do not think that advanced topics are not required for freshers. You never know what is waiting for you.
Do not follow just one DSA sheet. One sheet may have concepts which the other may not. Go with striver, babbar for DSA.
For CS fundamentals use Babbar, Kunal Kushwaha for OOPS.

Do competitive programming, use TLE eliminators for that. Use TLE post contest discussion, they usually have solutions of up to 4-5 problems. Even if you have a low rating, watch and solve the later problems as they involve some good concepts which can sometimes pop up in front of you, and your mind gets trained to handle tougher problems.
Keep your CGPA good enough, at least try to keep it above 8, it will help you to sit for all the companies.

Sometimes the outcome is not in your hands, you may not pass the OA even after completely solving all the questions (happened to me with Zeta). Just make peace with it and look for the next company. Don’t give a second thought to what is in the past. Don’t let it bother you.

Keep working and you will make it where you deserve. Hard work can never go in vain. Do not fall into that hardwork vs smartwork and all that superficial stuff. Keep it simple and drag yourself through it. Do not jumble yourself in tutorial hell, how to give interviews, how to smartly approach a problem, bla bla bla. Just be you and practice hard.

rounds.name: Online Assesment
rounds.description: This was conducted on the HirePro platform & duration was for 75mins. The test consisted of 3 sections, each with a time limit. The first section had 15 questions and was aptitude based wherein general questions on logical reasoning were asked. The second section had 25 technical questions based on Excel, CCN, OS, OOPs and Basic Statistics. The third section had 2 coding questions which were quite easy.

questions.text: How many elements are correctly sorted. Correct place means Rightly indexed when seen from a Sorted perspective. Ex: 1 3 2 4 5 sorted is 1 2 3 4 5 1 and 4 are in the correct place , whereas 3 and 2 are not in the correct place. So the result would be 2, 3 Since 2 are incorrect and 3 are correct

rounds.name: Technical Round 1
rounds.description: This round lasted for me around 45 mins to 1hr. I was the 1st person that was to be interviewed in my panel. It started with my introduction and then he directly jumped into a DSA problem it was related to cache so we had a buffer size of N and whenever we pushed an element it had a certain TTL (time_to_live) so suppose an element entered the buffer at 10:20 and its TTL was 2mins then at 10:23 it was supposed to be popped out of the cache and make room for other elements to enter. Initially i started with a hashmap solution but as soon as i started explaining i got the Priority Queue solution using heap here since my primary language was python he was checking my syntax or the function that i was mentioning with GFG and since in GFG the priority queue implementation was not the one using heap he started asking what is heap, heapify and balanced binary tree which i was able to explain it all. Then he started grilling me on GenAI and bit of ML since my entire resume was based on that

questions.text: DSA problem it was related to cache so we had a buffer size of N and whenever we pushed an element it had a certain TTL (time_to_live) so suppose an element entered the buffer at 10:20 and its TTL was 2mins then at 10:23 it was supposed to be popped out of the cache and make room for other elements to enter.
what is heap, heapify and balanced binary tree
Difference between GenAI and unsupervised learning (Generates new content and solely revolves around the input to find structure)
What is the output of unsupervised learning models (Clusters, Dimensionality Reduction)
Architecture of GenAI (Input layer + Tokenization + Embedding + Transformer + Attention Mechanism+ Decoder/output generator)
How does its matches the user context and generates an appropriate content (Semantic Similarity)
What is RAG
In a glimpse explain what is prompt engineering

Since i had explained RAG with the example of a medical chatbot he asked if a user prompts and says he cant concentrate in his work but the bot doesn't have any idea, as concentrate is not there in its DB then what will i do to give a proper response, initially i had said if at any point the bot cannot give a proper advice then i would have a default response wherein it will provide a general physician and he can take his concern forward with him but this wasn't what he had expected he said that the chatbot should ask few more questions on what he i feeling so that he can reach a conclusion and then provide a solution

Since my primary language was python they asked few questions based on that like types of exception handling in python and revolved around that more

Then they gave me a usecase kinda question like suppose there would be finger scanner for storing many peoples data what all would be your approaches. This was kind of an open ended question they wanted to see my how i would approach it (Here i would say ask whatever question you can possibly ask, coz more than the answer they want to see what you think so i asked what kind of data will be stored they said 0s and 1s i instantly started thinking in terms of FOSIP though i couldnt think much but mentioned few of the things that i could remember like grayscaling image optimization, thresholding and RLE and as i kept answering i even asked do we need to even process on the storage part for that they said you may so i mentioned a bit about the server and load balancing since they had said millions of data will be there and so on to retrieve as and when needed so but this a gist there was a detailed conversation on this)

tips.text: One thing i would advice is before asking your question first think properly if it is a proper question for your interviewer it would be kind of weird moment for you if he/she wont be able to answer.
In all your interviewees keep on asking their name coz though it didnt happen for me but for few they had asked who had interviewed them before

Be at your best behaviour and without realizing we end up doing those faces, like whenever we dont know an answer or even when we are definitely sure of an answer coz they do judge on basis of everything so keep a control on that as well.

Be well versed with your intro and the question to be asked be ready with that try to match it with your interest or the companies tech related, i always asked some question that was AI related or some projects where they were including AI or something like that so be prepared for that as well.

Whatever i had learnt i initially didnt make notes be it for my DSA or SQL or anything keep it ready so as soon as a company comes you then give time to prepare for researching about the company or anything extra you might need for preparing and not wasting on learning something which you had already did before.

And for internship here i was able to give a reason but it might not be acceptable for many people i thought if its unpaid then i might not get to learn anything its not true, but for that sake dont even pay for those fake internship there you get to do only those projects which are available on the youtube you get no industrial level experience

Before your interview dont keep on mugging up things coz when you try to learn in the last moment you end up messing other things which you would be well versed with, so calm down listen to some music and just revise whatever you have learnt so far.

And mainly i repeat dont get sad because you couldnt clear the interview ofc there you should have strong fundamentals but it also depends on luck too the only thing in your hand is to clear the OA the rest of the things you cant predict what happens next.
Keep practicing don't let your one failure mess up your other possible victory.
stay calm if you have put in your efforts then there is definitely a good company waiting for you.

tips.text: Be calm
Manage time smartly
Attack on low-hanging fruits first
Attempt questions which you are familiar first
Learn to leave lengthy questions
Don't get zoned out , every 1 minute has the same value :)
Never give up while giving interview

Even if you don't know, try to struggle with the question , tell the interviewers about your perspective, they are really interested more on how you think about approaching a problem , if you succeed in this way then this is really impressive

Sometimes you may even get a question that “hey AIML project is all about templates etc ”, that’s where you must say that while making a project it is also about proper lifecycle of development and building model , which task? Which model? Why this? Why not that etc ?
Never say anything negative , it may backfire you during the interview.
Don't break down,if your interviewer is an expert in a field like (cloud computing) and you have zero idea on that field , just be real-self.
Try to maintain a good CGPA , Mine was 9.86/10 which was quite impressive (in all 4 rounds)
Never say that I don't know , Try to understand any question , ask clarifying doubts and Try to connect the dots (It will really have a good impressive ,trust me)
Before your placement season starts , even if you code in X language(cpp) , learn about oops in Y (java) , Know about LLD , HLD also (system design).

Instead of depending on short notes for DBMS, CCN, OS etc , Study from standard Books (foreign authors like Korth , Navathe , Kurose , Tanenbaum or refer GATE lectures on YT ). Trust me it will really make you unique.
If given a chance to be back in time , I would focus on real time deployment , Cloud , Ports (Socket programming) and docker+kubernetes.
SQL QUESTIONS for Interviews (Do both Databases) just like Leetcode , Trust me you’ll like it , It has solutions section also.
Friendship with Language if you haven’t done DSA ever
Conceptual Clarity? if you know about your programming language.
If you know the drill of DSA : then Give Biweekly and weekly Leetcode contests, Never go for ratings, Never solve daily questions just for FOMO or BADGES , be real and truthful atleast with yourself.
JAVA and OOPS if you really want to answer with confident in interviews

If you want to crack your interview in one go ,(Study different System) : LLD Start with Snakes and Ladder and increase the complexity. Know about classes, interfaces , Getter , Setter, Constructor , extends , implements. Show modularity of code , try to write clean code and congrats you will never be rejected.
I have seen people doing Striver sheet etc , you may do it for DSA in your First year or second year.
Make sure to check Puzzles , as you may encounter them (sometimes)

It’s never late !?… Set time t=0 , and Start having “ honest consistency “ , GFG problem of the day? or Leetcode daily challenges (Or do daily problems but have a delay of 2 months like if today is 1 August 2025 , then solve the daily challenge problem of 1 June 2025).
Write code on pen-paper, Dry run , Draw recursive trees for DP. Follow one thing with full stewardship. Don't watch youtube lectures blindly.
